agents.note:
US-501 DONE (Sprint 69 / V0.29.24, first story). The dashboard header version chip is wired to .deploy-version: dashboard.html carries __DEPLOY_VERSION__ and the state server substitutes it in _injectHtml, next to the existing __SPLASH_TOKEN__ / __DISPLAY_AUTODIM__ / __DISPLAY_CAROUSEL__ seams. No JS reader -- one rule owns the chip. THE ONE CALL THE PM SHOULD KNOW ABOUT: the version is read PER REQUEST, not cached at handler construction the way the two config placeholders are. deploy-pi.sh restarts eclipse-states-http (step_install_state_server_units, line 1939) but stamps .deploy-version LAST (step_write_deploy_version, line 1955) -- deliberately, per US-354, so a failed restart cannot bump the stamp on a Pi running old code. A start-time cache would therefore have rendered the PREVIOUS deploy's version on EVERY deploy: green tests, correct-looking code, and the exact stale literal the story exists to delete. Mutation-proved -- caching makes the chip read V0.29.23 after V0.29.24 was stamped. Honest degrade: readDeployVersion returns None (never a guess) for no-path / absent / unreadable / malformed / missing / blank / non-string version, and the chip falls back to the SAME 'V?.?.?' sentinel the splash chip uses, so one glyph means 'unknown build' on both surfaces; the placeholder is always substituted so a raw __DEPLOY_VERSION__ can never reach the panel. NO deploy or unit-file change: --deploy-version-path defaults to '.deploy-version' WorkingDirectory-relative (same trick as --config, which ExecStart also omits), the unit runs as mcornelison from the repo root unsandboxed, and dashboard.html is already vouched so refresh_asset_dir will not prune it. 18 tests (15 RED-first, 3 markup guards mutation-proved after); tests/pi/splash + tests/ui + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py exit 0; ruff clean. CAVEAT for Iris: a file:// preview now shows raw __DEPLOY_VERSION__ in the chip -- the quoted-placeholder trick does not work on HTML text content; deliberate and dev-only. OWED: the on-Pi chip read after deploy. Sprint 69 is 1/10; next up is US-502 (power tile/bolt wiring).

PRIOR (Sprint 68, closed): BL-027 CLOSED on the code side (US-510 fast-follow, Marcus dispatch 2026-08-01). Iris's OFL Oswald subset (2,896 B; A-Z/0-9/space/hyphen, weight 600) is now inlined as a base64 @font-face. THE ONE CALL THE PM SHOULD KNOW ABOUT: the dispatch said to add the @font-face to tokens.css; I added it to BOTH tokens.css AND dashboard.css, because dashboard.html links ONLY dashboard.css -- an SSOT-only drop renders a fallback face on the Pi while every token/mirror test stays green, which is the exact two-correct-halves-that-stopped-agreeing failure (US-494/US-499). Pinned both ways. Stack is now 'Oswald','Arial Narrow',system-ui,sans-serif -- Bahnschrift + DIN Condensed LEFT deliberately: host-only faces mean a Windows dev box and the Pi render two different 'brand' faces, and Bahnschrift (unredistributable, absent from Pi OS) is why BL-027 existed. Weight tidy per step 3: .idle-wordmark 700->600, since a single-weight subset answers a 700 request with a SYNTHESISED bold (smeared condensed = looks like a rendering fault). OFL.txt copied into the kit AND vouched in deploy-pi.sh's dashboard asset list -- refresh_asset_dir PRUNES unvouched files, so an unvouched licence looks compliant in the repo while /opt/dashboard ships the face bare. 14 new pins in tests/ui/test_dashboard_brand_font_payload.py (payload decodes byte-for-byte to Iris's woff2; both copies identical; stack lead == embedded family; every bound rule asks 600; brand copy stays inside the cut subset; nothing fetched). 11 RED-first; the 3 born-green guards were mutation-proved after committing, 7 mutations total all RED, tree verified clean vs HEAD. Green in-loop: tests/ui + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py = 563 passed exit 0; ruff clean; bash -n on deploy-pi.sh clean. Architecture DoD met in-sprint (BL-027-CLOSED subsection under the two-file mirror). OWED, and it is ALL that is owed on Sprint 68: the ON-PI RENDER CHECK -- wordmark + card titles must show condensed Oswald, not generic sans. PM/CIO drill, not codeable. Sprint 68 is 6/6 with US-510's carveout now discharged.
